text:
Victor Alvarez: Heads up before we merge/apply the terraform bits for edge routing (PR redwood-terraform/913). I’m getting nervous about change mgmt here. This touches health-check based routing + DNS-ish primitives and could have blast radius if we fat-finger a target or TTL.

Irene Choi: +1. Anything that can move traffic cross-region needs stricter controls than our usual “2 approvals and ship”. What’s the plan for game day? Are we actually applying to prod infra or staging only?

Miles Thornton: For the first controlled failover game day we want to exercise the real automation path end-to-end. That includes the routing primitives the orchestrator will call. But we can scope to low-risk slice + “monitor-only” until we get confidence.

Rafael Mendes: SRE POV: we need a predictable change window, explicit approvers, and a rollback plan that doesn’t require heroics. Last incident we lost ~20 mins just coordinating who could push routing/DNS changes.

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet side: if this accidentally shifts more traffic than expected, we need to know which GPU pools are on the receiving end. Capacity headroom is not infinite. Don’t want terraform apply at random times.

Connor O'Brien: Release Eng here. We can treat this as a gated change: change ticket + scheduled window + sign-offs. For game day I’d prefer a “freeze except failover changes” window so we aren’t contending with other deploys.

Emily Zhao: Also note the network probes/synthetic checks can be noisy. If the routing health checks are wired wrong we can cause oscillation even without an actual outage.

Victor Alvarez: Exactly. Current terraform module sets health checks + weighted targets. If a health check goes “unhealthy” because of probe noise, it can start moving traffic. We need guardrails.

Irene Choi: Let’s enumerate the guardrails we want:
- Required reviewers: Infra Networking (me or Victor) + SRE (Rafael or Miles) for any terraform that modifies edge routing records/targets.
- Apply window: only during a scheduled change window with on-call present.
- Rollback: pre-generated revert plan + tested in staging.

Mina Haddad: Routing team chiming in: the orchestrator can be feature-flagged and scoped, but the underlying routing primitives still matter. We should gate any “automatic” behavior behind the orchestrator flag AND keep edge routing changes conservative.

Aisha Bello: From alerting side: please avoid doing this during peak. If we trigger burn-rate alerts during the game day it’ll page half the org unless we temporarily annotate/suppress (with explicit approval).

Connor O'Brien: Proposal for game day change window:
- Wed 10:00–12:00 PT (avoid Fri)
- Freeze: no unrelated prod terraform applies during that window
- Required sign-offs before window starts: Infra + SRE + Release Eng
- Live comms: #incidents + this thread linked, even if it’s “planned”

Rafael Mendes: Works for me. Also want: “two-person rule” for terraform apply: one driver, one verifier reading out plan diffs.

Victor Alvarez: +1. Can we require posting `terraform plan` output (sanitized) in the thread before apply? At least the diff summary.

Connor O'Brien: Yes. Checklist-style:
1) `terraform init` / workspace check (prod vs staging)
2) `terraform plan -out=tfplan` and paste diff summary
3) Verifier confirms expected: only intended records/targets, no unrelated drift
4) Apply
5) Immediate validation: check health checks status, traffic split metrics, error rate/latency dashboards
6) Keep rollback command ready (or revert commit + apply)

Vanessa Ortiz: Add capacity check step before apply. Harish has the authoritative numbers but we should at least confirm “N% headroom” in target region for the slice.

Harish Reddy: Yep. For game day, please ping me day-before with the expected max % shift and which model pools. I can confirm headroom and any ongoing maintenance. During window I can be on standby.

Miles Thornton: On scope: for the first run we’re failing over only a low-risk route group (internal + a few sandbox tenants) and only up to 5% progressive shift. The orchestrator will enforce hold-down timers. Terraform is just enabling the routing primitives; actual traffic shift is via the orchestrator.

Emily Zhao: TTL question: are we changing TTLs as part of terraform? If TTL is too high, rollback is slow.

Victor Alvarez: Module currently sets TTL 60s for the records used by the orchestrator-controlled failover. Existing default is 300s in some places. I’d like to standardize at 60s for game day-targeted records.

Irene Choi: 60s is fine for these records. But we should NOT blanket-lower TTL for unrelated zones. Keep the blast radius small.

Connor O'Brien: Agree. Also: if TTL changes need propagation time, we should do TTL lowering in a separate change at least 24h prior to the actual failover window.

Rafael Mendes: Yes please. TTL lowering 24h prior reduces “why didn’t it move?” confusion in the moment.

Aisha Bello: If we’re doing TTL lowering, can we annotate dashboards so folks don’t misinterpret the small traffic changes during propagation as “something’s wrong”.

Mina Haddad: On review requirements: can we formalize in CODEOWNERS for the terraform module path? That way GitHub enforces Infra + SRE review.

Victor Alvarez: I can add CODEOWNERS entries for `modules/edge-routing/*` to require @infra-networking and @sre-reviewers.

Irene Choi: Do it. And for applies, let’s limit who has permissions to the prod workspace. At minimum, only Infra on-call + Release Eng + named SRE leads.

Connor O'Brien: I can coordinate with INT-881 folks to ensure RBAC is aligned. But for game day: driver should be Victor (infra) with Connor as verifier or vice versa.

Miles Thornton: SRE side we’ll have an IC and a dedicated observer. IC will approve go/no-go, but the apply driver can be infra.

Vanessa Ortiz: Please also add an explicit stop condition: if target region queue depth or GPU saturation crosses threshold X, we pause/rollback.

Harish Reddy: I’ll send suggested thresholds for headroom and queue depth. In general, if headroom <15% on the receiving pool, we shouldn’t proceed.

Rafael Mendes: Summarizing agreement (unless objections):
- Terraform/edge routing changes are “high risk” and require Infra + SRE review (CODEOWNERS enforced)
- Separate change window for prod applies; no drive-by applies
- For game day: Wed 10–12 PT, freeze unrelated prod infra changes
- Two-person rule on apply + post plan diff + capacity check pre-flight
- TTL lowering change 24h before, scoped only to failover-related records
- Rollback plan prepped and rehearsed in staging

Irene Choi: This matches what I want. Victor, can you own CODEOWNERS + split TTL change into separate PR? Connor, can you get the change window onto the calendar + confirm freeze comms?

Victor Alvarez: Yep. I’ll update PR 913 with CODEOWNERS + carve out TTL PR. Also will add a README section: “Do not apply outside scheduled windows; post plan; two-person verification”.

Connor O'Brien: On it. I’ll draft the change ticket + announce the window in #eng-releases + link the game day checklist.

Aisha Bello: If you share the exact window I’ll prep a dashboard annotation + note for on-call so alerts are interpreted correctly.

Miles Thornton: Thanks all. This makes the automation story much more credible. We’ll reference this agreement in the game day plan/runbook too.
